unconsolidated_missing_candidate_preview.context: Commutative algebra: quotient ring A/I of a commutative unital ring A by an ideal I, with elements additive cosets a+I, operations induced from A and canonical surjective unital quotient map A→A/I. This includes prime-ideal quotients, polynomial-ring quotients and ideal-power quotients; a quotient's being a field, local ring or R-algebra requires additional conditions.

Commutative algebra: polynomial algebra R[X_i : i in I] over a commutative unital coefficient ring R, for an arbitrary set I of independent indeterminates; each polynomial has finite monomial support. Includes the one-variable and finite-variable cases and polynomial algebras over fields and quotient coefficient rings.
Commutative algebra and algebraic geometry: residue field A/m of a commutative local ring (A,m), including the prime-localized κ(p)=R_p/pR_p and the scheme-point κ(s)=O_{S,s}/m_s.
unconsolidated_missing_candidate_preview.surface_phrase: residue field of a local ring

unconsolidated_missing_candidate_preview.context: Module theory: quotient left R-module M/N by an R-submodule N, whose elements are additive cosets m+N with addition and R-scalar action induced by M. Includes ideal modules I/I², successive filtration quotient modules and regular-module quotients R/I; extra ring, graded, flatness, or field structure is not part of this quotient-module meaning.

Set theory: preimage or inverse image of subset B⊆Y under an arbitrary function f:X→Y, defined as f^{-1}[B]={x∈X:f(x)∈B}; notation f^{-1}[B] never presupposes that f is invertible. Includes underlying set preimages of open/measurable sets and contractions of prime ideals under ring homomorphisms, where additional structure is a separate condition.

Category theory: ordinary category with objects, morphisms, identities and associative composition, without requiring its collection of objects to be a set; any size assumptions are stated separately.
Commutative algebra: commutative ring with multiplicative identity
Set theory: injectivity of an arbitrary map f:X→Y, meaning f(x)=f(y) implies x=y for all x,y in X; for structured maps this is the underlying-set condition.
Commutative algebra: commutative unital algebra A over a specified base field k, with a chosen unital structure homomorphism k→A; A need not be a field, a domain or geometrically regular.
unconsolidated_missing_candidate_preview.surface_phrase: commutative unital algebra over a field

unconsolidated_missing_candidate_preview.context: Set theory: power set of an arbitrary underlying set X, namely the collection of all subsets of X; variable names X and S are interchangeable.

Commutative algebra: evaluation R-algebra homomorphism ev_(a_i):R[X_i : i∈I]→A into a commutative unital R-algebra A, sending each formal indeterminate X_i to a specified a_i∈A and fixing the coefficients through the structure map R→A; includes univariate evaluation f(a) and the canonical R[X_s:s∈S]→S sending X_s to s.

Commutative algebra: product IJ of two ideals of a commutative unital ring R, generated by finite sums of pairwise products; ordinary ideal powers I^n for n≥1 by repeated ideal multiplication, and by convention I^0=R when nonnegative exponents are used.

Point-set topology: quotient (final) topology induced by a surjective continuous map q:X→Q, where U⊆Q is open exactly when q^{-1}(U) is open in X; includes canonical quotient-set maps and the map X→f(X) when equipped with final topology, independently of whether a larger codomain Y is surjected onto.
unconsolidated_missing_candidate_preview.surface_phrase: quotient topology on Y for f

unconsolidated_missing_candidate_preview.context: Module theory: finite-rank free left R-module R^n over a unital ring R for finite n≥0, the direct sum of n copies of the regular left R-module, with its canonical standard basis; not the same as an arbitrary locally free module.

Set theory: surjective function f:X→Y whose image is the entire stated codomain Y; for module homomorphisms this is the underlying-set surjectivity of the R-linear map, independent of linearity, free domain, or choice of basis.

Commutative algebra: kernel ideal of a unital homomorphism φ:A→B of commutative rings, consisting of all a∈A mapped to 0_B; for a polynomial evaluation map it is the ideal of polynomial relations, and for a quotient-localization composite it is the inverse image of zero in the target ring.
Module theory: an R-module admitting a finite or countably infinite set of generators under R-linear combinations; no projectivity, flatness, or finitely-generated-only condition.
Commutative algebra: subset S of a commutative unital ring R, containing 1_R and closed under multiplication, used as denominators in ring or module localization.
Commutative algebra: principal ideal generated by one element

Category theory: ordinary comma category of functors F:A→C, G:B→C, whose objects are triples (a,b,u:F(a)→G(b)) and morphisms are compatible commuting squares. Includes (j↓H) and (H↓j) with their opposite arrow directions as different instances; no assumption u is invertible.

Category theory: slice (over-)category C/U of a category C over an object U, with objects morphisms V→U and arrows commuting over U; a special ordinary comma-category construction but not the same concept as the general comma category or the existing iso-comma construction.

Module theory: submodule generated by a subset S of a left R-module M, consisting of all finite R-linear combinations of elements of S; for a finite S={m_1,...,m_n} this is the finite R-linear span Σ_i R m_i, possibly all of M.

Module theory over a commutative unital ring R: ideal action IM on an R-module M, the R-submodule generated by all finite sums of products i*m with i∈I and m∈M; this includes (I^n)M for ideal powers I^n, but differs from ideal multiplication I^n alone and from forming a quotient module M/I^nM.
Category theory: ordinary covariant functor F:I→C from a small indexing category I to an arbitrary locally small target category C; no smallness requirement on C.
